Luxury Candle Gift Box Packaging: A Design and Sourcing Guide

Published August 19, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Candle brands should specify a rigid or folding box with an inner footprint 3-6 mm larger than the jar, plus a cutout insert (greyboard or EVA) that cups the base so the glass cannot shift. Leave clear warnings about burning on the pack, and ask suppliers whether their inks and coatings meet food-contact-adjacent or low-migration expectations, since regulatory status varies by market. MOQ 500-1,000 pieces, samples 7-10 days, bulk 20-30 days.

Match the format to the jar

Square rigid boxes suit 8-12 oz jars and leave room for a sturdy insert; round formats cost more because curved walls are harder to wrap and assemble. For folding cartons, use 350-400 gsm CCNB with a glued crash-lock or tuck-end bottom. Always size the interior to the widest point of the jar, including the lid collar, with 3-6 mm clearance so the label does not scuff during insertion.

Inserts that hold glass securely

A one-piece greyboard or 2.0 mm EVA insert with a circular cutout at the jar base diameter plus 1-2 mm is the standard solution; add a second cutout layer for the neck if the jar is tall. Confirm insert depth tolerance of ±1 mm and run a 60-80 cm drop test on a packed sample, since glass breakage in transit is the most common candle-box complaint.

Heat, flame and compliance notes

Boxes sit away from the flame in normal use, but buyers should still confirm that inks, foils and coatings are low-migration where required and that warning copy (never leave a burning candle unattended) is printed or on a leaflet. Requirements differ by country, so request supplier certificates and consult a compliance specialist for each target market rather than assuming one approval covers all.

Budgeting MOQ and lead time

Plan 500-1,000 pieces per SKU for rigid candle boxes and 3,000-5,000 for folding cartons. Samples take 7-10 days; bulk production 20-30 days after sign-off. If the design uses a foil-stamped logo or soft-touch lamination, confirm those processes at the quoting stage because they extend lead time by 3-5 days.

Buyer checklist

  1. Size interior to the widest jar point with 3-6 mm clearance
  2. Specify a greyboard or EVA insert cutout with ±1 mm tolerance
  3. Request a 60-80 cm drop test on a fully packed sample
  4. Confirm warning copy placement and coating suitability for target markets
  5. Lock finish choices (foil, soft-touch) before quoting to protect lead time

Frequently asked questions

What clearance should the insert leave around a candle jar?

Allow 3-6 mm between jar and box wall and cut the base cutout 1-2 mm larger than the jar bottom. This keeps the glass stable without scuffing labels during insertion.

Do candle boxes need fire-retardant materials?

In normal use the box is not exposed to flame, so standard greyboard and coated paper are typical. The critical asks are stable inserts, warning copy and low-migration inks where required; confirm with a compliance advisor per market.

What is the MOQ for custom candle boxes?

Rigid formats start at 500-1,000 pieces per SKU; folding cartons with inserts typically start at 3,000-5,000 pieces. Sample lead time is 7-10 days and bulk production 20-30 days.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Candle boxes need structure that survives glass weight and a finish that sells the scent. Rigid boxes from 1200/1500/1800 gsm greyboard wrapped in 157 gsm art paper or specialty papers hold heavier products; EVA foam inserts (20–60 density) cradle the candle. Finishes of matte lamination, soft-touch, hot foil and embossing set the premium tone. The box passes a 24 h static load test based on product weight. MOQ is 500 PCS per size and artwork, with corner gap ≤ 1.5 mm and lid-base fit 1.0–1.8 mm.

Frequently Asked Questions

What insert protects a glass candle?

EVA foam at 20–60 density with a die-cut cavity keeps the glass jar stable in transit.

What finish works for candle boxes?

Soft-touch lamination with hot foil or embossing is the standard premium candle-box combination.
